# T5.01: where the time goes (and why the GPU copy path is off for now)

`tools/tilebench W H N`: `enc_load_nv12` (CPU tiling into the input surface) and `enc_encode` (doorbell to
semaphore), 1 ref, constant QP, frames 3..N averaged:

| size | tiling | encode | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1920x1080 | 0.78 ms (max 1.08) | 1.08 ms | 1.87 ms |
| 3840x2160 | **5.31 ms** (max 7.53) | 3.90 ms | 9.20 ms |

The tiler is the bigger cost at 4K: it computes the address and does a 16-byte `memcpy` per run.

Before starting on a GPU input path, checked whether NVENC can read anything a copy engine can produce (the
experimental `encode1` of d56225c, 256x128):

| input data | input_cfg | luma PSNR |
|---|---|---|
| measured NVENC layout | block_height 2 | 45.25 dB |
| classic GOB (`bl_tile_plane`), bh 1/2/3 | input_bl_mode 0/1/2 | 9.9-13.4 dB (bit-identical across input_bl_mode) |
| pitch-linear | block_height 0-5, tiled_16x16 | 9.5-9.6 dB |

So `input_bl_mode` is ignored on Ada, and only NVENC's own layout works. The copy engine writes the classic GOB
layout, so it can't do the conversion in one pass. M5 is re-planned in tasks.md: fast CPU tiling and asynchronous
encoding first; a GPU (Metal compute) swizzle later.
